title: Three points, a bigger payment
hook: A mortgage rate moves from 4% to 7%. Does the monthly payment move by about 3%?

knows: that a loan has a monthly payment
doesNotKnow: that a few points of rate change the payment by far more than a few percent

misconception: Rates up from 4% to 7% add about 3% to the payment.
objective: The learner can explain that three points of rate on a 30-year loan raise the payment by about 39%, because interest is charged on every dollar owed for decades.

claims.text: A $300,000 loan over 30 years (360 level monthly payments) at 4% a year has a payment of $1,432.25.
At 7% a year the same loan has a payment of $1,995.91.
The payment at 7% is 39% higher than at 4% (1,995.91 / 1,432.25 = 1.394).
The rate rising from 4% to 7% is a 75% rise as a ratio (7 / 4 - 1), which is not the rise in the payment.
The first month's interest on $300,000 is $1,000 at 4% and $1,750 at 7%.
The lesson is a model: fixed rate, fixed 30-year term, level payments, illustrative rates, not a forecast and not advice.
claims.source: Assumptions of Demo.tsx; stage chip 'Model: $300,000, 30 years, fixed rate'.

recall.question: A $200,000 loan over 30 years has a payment of $1,074 at 5%. At 8%, the payment rises by closest to which?
recall.why: At 8% the payment is $1,468, 37% more (1,467.53 / 1,073.64). Interest is charged on every dollar owed for decades, so three points lift the payment far more than 3%, though less than the 60% rise of the rate as a ratio (8 / 5).
